officialTitle: Lurbinectedin as second-line treatment for patients with small-cell lung cancer: a single-arm, open-label, phase 2 basket trial

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between Oct 16, 2015, and Jan 15, 2019, 105 patients were enrolled and treated with lurbinectedin.
design.notes: Single-arm phase 2 basket trial; SCLC cohort with one prior chemotherapy-containing line, ECOG PS 2 or lower, no brain metastases. Evidence is non-comparative.

clinicalQuestion: What is the activity and safety of lurbinectedin monotherapy as second-line treatment for SCLC after platinum-based chemotherapy?

pico.population: Adults with SCLC after one prior chemotherapy-containing line, no brain metastases

arms.label: Lurbinectedin
arms.dosing: 3.2 mg/m2 as a 1-h intravenous infusion every 3 weeks
arms.doseSourceQuote: Treatment consisted of 3·2 mg/mlurbinectedin administered as a 1-h intravenous infusion every 3 weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

publications.title: Lurbinectedin as second-line treatment for patients with small-cell lung cancer: a single-arm, open-label, phase 2 basket trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Between Oct 16, 2015, and Jan 15, 2019, 105 patients were enrolled and treated with lurbinectedin. Median follow-up was 17·1 months (IQR 6·5-25·3). Overall response by investigator assessment was seen in 37 patients (35·2%; 95% CI 26·2-45·2).

safety.sourceQuote: The most common grade 3-4 adverse events (irrespective of causality) were haematological abnormalities-namely, anaemia (in nine [9%] patients), leucopenia (30 [29%]), neutropenia (48 [46%]), and thrombocytopenia (seven [7%]).

Serious treatment-related adverse events occurred in 11 (10%) patients, of which neutropenia and febrile neutropenia were the most common (five [5%] patients for each). No treatment-related deaths were reported.

strengths: Prospective multicentre trial in a population with few options
limitations: Single-arm phase 2 evidence; no randomised comparator
Response assessed by investigators rather than central review in the primary endpoint

clinicalImplications.text: Single-arm phase 2 data showed activity of lurbinectedin monotherapy in relapsed SCLC with mainly haematological toxicity; the evidence is non-comparative.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Single-arm evidence only: patients with brain metastases were excluded, so extrapolation to them is uncertain.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 32224306.
